newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Auridiam upgrades PNG gold deposit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Auridiam upgrades PNG gold deposit.

text.p: Gold and diamond miner Auridiam Consolidated NL said on Monday that it had upgraded the resource estimate at its Woodlark Island gold project in Papua New Guinea to 344,000 ounces of gold from 195,000 ounces.
Woodlark Island is located in the Solomon Sea, 600 km east of Port Moresby and 150 km north of Misima Island.
Auridiam won a tender for an option to develop the deposit late last year from Highlands Gold NL.
Auridiam said it was at the stage of a final feasibility study and discussions with landowners had started and social, metallurgical and engineering consultants had been appointed.

"Subject to the feasibility study and the necessary approvals, the company intends to proceed to development in 1997 with an estimated construction time of less than one year," Auridiam said in a statement.
The company said its drilling at the project had found high grade mineralisation near the surface which increased the likelihood of an early pay back in a mining operation.

"The new resource estimates are contained within fairly constrained areas and Auridiam envisages that quite low (less than three to one) stripping ratios will allow the majority of the resources to be converted into mineable reserves," the company said.
It also said that early metallurgical studies had confirmed the amenability of the ores to standard metallurgical extraction.

Under the option agreement with Highlands, Auridiam can elect to purchase the project's title for a A$850,000, payable in quarterly instalments. In addition, a royalty of A$10 per ounce to a maximum of 200,000 ounces is payable on production.
Auridiam paid an initial sum of A$150,000 for an option to evaluate the deposit.
At 2.50 p.m. (0450 GMT), Auridiam shares were one cent firmer at 71 cents.
